native_language_semantic_policy: One-dimensional Python NumPy float64 array is represented by a one-dimensional native R double vector. Python ValueError maps to native R error conditions. The explicit extra python_boundary_mode selects frozen-source nonfinite and dtype coercions while ordinary native R defaults stay strictly finite.
reviewer_statement: Author-side six-domain review of deterministic native trapezoid rule against frozen Python 1.2 source: required and optional argument mapping, standard one-dimensional numeric and representable scalar-container casts, nonfinite and invalid time grids, normalization truthiness, exception accept-reject boundaries, output shape and float64 values, and scientific integral weight estimand. Direct frozen Python numerical oracles and deterministic randomized algebra fixtures passed. This is native-language mathematical/accepted-domain semantic equivalence, NOT Python ndarray identity, arbitrary Python extension-object protocols, Python warning or exception class identity, independent reviewer approval, or CRAN release readiness.

case_evidence.description: Required time and default false normalization; opt-in source boundary mode and two-point minimum.
Native 1-D ndarray analogues, floats, integers, Booleans, numeric text, mixed scalar list and complex ndarray-to-real casting; scalar and one-element normalization arrays.
180 seeded strictly increasing finite grids, source NumPy direct differentials, nonfinite propagation, normalized and unnormalized weights.
Rejected empty, scalar, matrix, higher-rank, repeated/decreasing/NaN grids and ambiguous multi-element array flags; Python ValueError to R error mapping.
One dimensional numeric vector of float64 trapezoid weights preserving grid order and allowed nonfinite outputs; native R representation of source NumPy ndarray.
Exact trapezoidal quadrature, denominator normalization, and complex NumPy casting, with no interpolation or resampling.

known_language_specific_limits: R native numeric vector is not a Python ndarray object
Python custom __array__ and __bool__ user object protocols are not native R coercion methods
Native R condition and warning classes are not Python exception and NumPy warning classes
